title: OOP Powering CI3: Controllers & Models Are Just PHP Classes
description: See how CI3's Controllers and Models are built entirely from ordinary PHP OOP — the same class, constructor, encapsulation, and inheritance rules Java uses too.
congratsText: Nothing about CI3 is magic — it's the OOP you already know, applied to Controllers and Models!
objectives: Explain why `class Menu extends CI_Controller` is ordinary PHP inheritance, not CI3-specific syntax.
Explain what parent::__construct() sets up in a CI3 controller's constructor chain.
Apply private-property encapsulation to a CI3 model's table or connection details.
Diagnose a broken controller caused by a missing parent::__construct() call.
Trace a multi-level extends chain from CI_Controller through a custom base controller to a page controller.
recap: class Menu extends CI_Controller uses PHP's ordinary extends keyword — CI3 didn't invent special controller syntax.
A controller's parent::__construct() call runs CI_Controller's own setup, including what makes $this->load and sessions work.
CI3 models apply the same private-property, public-method encapsulation as any well-built PHP class, just for database access.
Skipping parent::__construct() breaks CI3's setup even when the class declaration and extends line are both correct.
CI3 projects commonly layer inheritance — Menu extends MY_Controller extends CI_Controller — using the same multi-level extends chain PHP and Java both support.

sections.title: A Controller Is Just a PHP Class

chunks.text: When you write class Menu extends CI_Controller, you're not writing framework-specific syntax — it's the same class X extends Y pattern from ordinary PHP OOP.

check.question: Is `extends CI_Controller` special CI3-only syntax?
options: No, it's standard PHP class inheritance
Yes, CI3 invented its own keyword

chunks.text: CI_Controller itself is nothing mysterious — it's a plain PHP class sitting in CodeIgniter's system folder, with its own properties and methods like any other class.

check.question: Is CI_Controller a special non-class construct?
options: No, it's an ordinary PHP class
Yes, it's compiled framework magic

chunks.text: That means everything you already know about a PHP class — properties, methods, visibility — applies to every controller you write.

check.question: Do normal PHP class rules apply inside a controller?
options: Yes, fully
No, controllers follow separate rules

quiz.question: Which statement is true about `class Menu extends CI_Controller`?
options: It's ordinary PHP inheritance, same as any subclass
CI3 replaces PHP's extends keyword with its own syntax
extends only works for controllers, not other PHP classes
CI_Controller is a PHP interface, not an actual class

chunks.text: A controller's constructor almost always opens with one line: parent::__construct(); — calling CI_Controller's own constructor before anything else runs.

check.question: Does a controller's constructor usually call the parent's constructor first?
options: Yes, as its first line
No, CI3 calls it automatically

chunks.text: That line is the same parent:: pattern from plain PHP inheritance — CI3 didn't invent a special startup hook, it's just OOP.

check.question: Is parent::__construct() unique CI3 syntax?
options: No, it's standard PHP inheritance syntax
Yes, only CI3 controllers use it

chunks.text: Skip that call, and everything CI_Controller's constructor was supposed to set up — like $this->load — never gets initialized.

check.question: What happens if that parent call is skipped?
options: CI_Controller's setup never runs
Nothing changes, it's optional

quiz.question: Arrange the tokens to build the first two lines of a correct CI3 controller constructor.

chunks.text: A CI3 model follows the same encapsulation habit as any well-built PHP class: keep the table name or connection details private, and expose behavior through public methods.

check.question: Should a model's raw table name usually be private?
options: Yes, exposed only through methods
No, it should always be public

chunks.text: A typical model constructor sets a private property like $table and still opens with parent::__construct(); — the same chain from the last section, now protecting data instead of a view.

check.question: Does a model's constructor use the same parent:: pattern as a controller?
options: Yes, the identical pattern
No, models skip parent::

chunks.text: None of this is CI3-specific — it's the exact private-property, public-method encapsulation habit from plain PHP OOP, just applied to database access.

check.question: Is model encapsulation a CI3-only concept?
options: No, it's standard PHP encapsulation
Yes, it's unique to models

quiz.question: Type the access modifier a well-encapsulated CI3 model would use for a property like $table, so outside code can't touch it directly.

chunks.text: Picture a controller that extends CI_Controller correctly but whose constructor never calls parent::__construct(); — the class declaration is fine, but the chain is broken.

check.question: Is the class declaration itself the problem here?
options: No, the missing parent call is
Yes, extends is written wrong

chunks.text: $this->load, sessions, and other CI3 setup all depend on that call — without it, $this->load->view() throws an error, even though the controller "extends" correctly.

check.question: Can $this->load work without that parent call?
options: No, it depends on that call
Yes, extends alone is enough

chunks.text: This is the same failure a Java subclass would hit skipping super() when the parent constructor sets up something the subclass needs — the language differs, the bug doesn't.

check.question: Would a similar bug happen in Java skipping super()?
options: Yes, the same kind of failure
No, Java doesn't have this issue

quiz.question: This controller extends CI_Controller correctly. What's actually broken?
options: A missing parent::__construct() call
extends CI_Controller is the wrong keyword here
load->model() is not a real CI3 method at all
PHP refuses to parse a class with a commented line

chunks.text: Real CI3 projects often add one more layer: a MY_Controller that extends CI_Controller, and then every page controller extends MY_Controller instead.

check.question: Does adding MY_Controller remove the extends chain to CI_Controller?
options: No, MY_Controller still extends CI_Controller
Yes, it replaces CI_Controller entirely

chunks.text: That's ordinary multi-level inheritance — Menu extends MY_Controller, MY_Controller extends CI_Controller — the same layering Java supports with any chain of subclasses.

check.question: Can PHP chain more than one level of inheritance like this?
options: Yes, multi-level inheritance is normal
No, PHP allows only one level

chunks.text: Each constructor in that chain still calls its own parent::__construct();, so the setup passes all the way down from CI_Controller to your final page controller.

check.question: Does each layer still need its own parent:: call?
options: Yes, every layer in the chain
No, only the top layer needs it

quiz.question: Arrange the tokens to show the correct extends chain, from the framework's base class down to a page controller.
